title: Why 10 Days Vanished From the Calendar in 1582 (Leap Years)
description:
In 1582 the calendar skipped ten days to fix a drift against the seasons, and the century-year leap rule (divisible by 400) keeps the average year at 365.2425 days.

The drift ring is illustrative and exaggerated. Only Catholic lands switched in 1582; Britain waited until 1752 and Russia until 1918.

Narration is a synthetic voice (VoiceStudio). Animation is written as code.
